messages.author: e5d0b3c2486cd4e3
messages.subject: Adding an arbitrary legend
parts:
Below is an example of some data I have and the chart I'm producing. Note that the legend produced by ggplot has 10 rows with 2 colors. However, in my real problem I don't really care about the 10 groups. Rather I only want a legend for my.data$type. So I would like to suppress the default legend and add one that has only two colors with Type I and Type II. Any suggestions, clean or hacky, would be greatly appreciated.

con <- textConnection("
   index which.date       date
1      1 start.date 2010-11-01
2      1   end.date 2011-01-31
3      2 start.date 2010-11-03
4      2   end.date 2010-12-01
5      3 start.date 2011-02-01
6      3   end.date 2011-04-30
7      4 start.date 2011-02-01
8      4   end.date 2011-04-30
9      5 start.date 2011-02-01
10     5   end.date 2011-03-02
11     6 start.date 2011-02-03
12     6   end.date 2011-04-30
13     7 start.date 2011-02-12
14     7   end.date 2011-05-12
15     8 start.date 2011-02-17
16     8   end.date 2011-02-20
17     9 start.date 2011-02-23
18     9   end.date 2011-04-30
19    10 start.date 2011-03-01
20    10   end.date 2011-03-31
")
my.data <- read.table(con, header = TRUE, row.names = 1, skip = 1)
my.data$date <- as.Date(my.data$date)
close(con)

library(ggplot2)
col <- rep(c("cornflowerblue", "mediumvioletred"), each = 5)
gg <- ggplot(my.data, aes(date, index))
gg <- gg + geom_line(aes(colour = factor(index)), size = 2)
gg <- gg + scale_colour_manual(value = col)

gg

messages.author: d34d025a513c07fc
messages.subject: Re: Adding an arbitrary legend
parts:
Instead of trying to set the colors of each item directly, you should add a column that specifies the group, and map it to colour:

my.data$mygroup <- rep(c("Type I", "Type II"), each = 10)

ggplot(my.data, aes(date, index)) + 
    geom_line(aes(colour=mygroup, group=index), size = 2) + 
    scale_colour_manual(value = c("cornflowerblue", "mediumvioletred"))


-Winston
